commits.pr_title: [Feature][Quantization] Gather MiMo fused-QKV FP8 rows exactly by default
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR upstreams work from the patch set of the MiMo recipe we deploy — Diffbot's MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL FP8KV/W4A8 recipe (Hugging Face: diffbot/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL-FP8KV-W4A8-2x-RTX-PRO-6000, built by Mike Tung), itself porting parts from the local-inference-lab/vllm fork: the idea and the original implementation belong to the recipe's authors, not to us. Their version of this change is tracked in local-inference-lab/vllm#874; we re-derived the diff against upstream main, wrote or extended the tests, and ran the checks.

### Motivation

`_shard_fp8_qkv_proj` re-quantizes every gathered row through a dequantize-requantize round trip whenever `tp_size != ckpt_tp`: the fallback re-derives each block scale in fp32 and only reproduces the checkpoint's bytes when rounding cooperates.

When `ckpt_tp` is a multiple of `tp_size`, the rank's rows can be taken from the checkpoint byte-for-byte instead, in two shapes:

- **Block-aligned segments** (MiMo SWA chunks: 3712 = 29 x 128 rows, all three segments multiples of 128): a pure block permutation — gather the rows directly, no arithmetic, no scale re-derivation.
- **Straddling segments** (GA/Pro chunks: a 192-row K segment, one and a half scale blocks): each owned chunk keeps its K and V rows together, zero-padded to a whole block count, so every row still carries its checkpoint scale — the rank's parameter becomes the zero-padded `[Q_1 | ... | Q_g | K_1 V_1 pad | ... | K_g V_g pad]` layout, built as a `MergedColumnParallelLinear` instead of a de-interleaved `QKVParallelLinear`. The forward splits that padded output back per chunk. A checkpoint whose scales form one continuous grid (rather than one grid per chunk) fails loudly with a `ValueError` naming the precondition instead of dying in a shape assert at load.

Layouts failing the divisor or Q-segment alignment conjunct keep the existing path unchanged.

The exact gather is now the default: it is selected by geometry alone, so a rank whose layout qualifies takes checkpoint rows byte-for-byte. A padded layout whose scales are not per chunk now raises instead of silently requantizing. Four signed commits: the block-permutation gather with its tests, the padded gather for straddling segments, the module wiring with its round-trip test, and the removal of the environment gate.

### Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for `mimo qkv fp8`, `exact fp8 qkv gather`, and `mimo exact qkv` (zero hits). The open PRs in this loader area, verified against their pages, are orthogonal:

- #58142 keeps fused-QKV pairing state across weight-loading calls (edits `load_weights`);
- #58184 skips fused-QKV tensors for absent layers (edits `load_weights`);
- #46755 adds TP > num_kv_heads head replication (edits `_shard_fp8_qkv_proj`).

None changes the row-selection math for `tp_size < ckpt_tp`. Re-running `gh search` immediately before opening this PR returned no matching PR.

## Test Plan

```bash
ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py vllm/envs.py tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py
ruff check vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py vllm/envs.py tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/quantization/test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py -v
```

## Test Result

Results: **31 passed, 2 skipped** — the 19 pre-existing sharding tests, unchanged, plus:

- `test_exact_gather_permutes_checkpoint_rows` (SWA geometry, tp 1 and 2): weights and scales byte-identical to the checkpoint rows the rank owns;
- `test_exact_padded_layout_matches_checkpoint` (GA and Pro geometries, tp below `ckpt_tp`): every weight byte equal to the checkpoint's `[Q | K V pad]` order with zero pad rows, and every scale row in the padded order;
- `test_split_qkv_round_trips_the_padded_layout` (GA and Pro, tp below `ckpt_tp`): `_split_qkv` on the transposed rank slice returns exactly the checkpoint rows the rank owns, byte for byte — pinning the writer's padded order to the reader's so a one-sided layout change cannot slip through with shapes intact.

The 2 skips are `tp_size >= ckpt_tp` cases of the padded tests: the plain-chunk path covers that region, not the padded one. `test_flag_off_keeps_requantizing_loader` went away with the gate; the requantizing loader keeps its coverage in `test_fused_qkv_proj_sharding` at `tp_size=8`.

`pre-commit run` itself cannot execute in this NixOS environment (hook environments fail with the `stub-ld` dynamic-linker error), so the repo-pinned ruff 0.14.0 was run directly.

**No model eval was run.** The exact gather takes checkpoint rows without arithmetic and is now the default for the geometries that qualify, so a deployment should compare its outputs against a requantizing build on its own model before rollout — that comparison is not part of this PR.

## AI Assistance

AI assistance was used (pi coding agent): analysis, draft, and test runs were produced by the agent; the human author reviewed every changed line, ran the checks above, and defends the change end-to-end.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Move Multimodal Processor, KV Connectors, LoRA, Spec Decode Draft and three more steps from fixed to automatic shards
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Moves seven steps, and their AMD mirrors, from fixed pytest shards to `automatic_shard`, as #61200, #61477 and #62077 did for others. For each: `parallelism` is dropped, `--shard-id`/`--num-shards` come off the commands, `Shard %N` / `%N` comes out of the label (the generator adds `shard N/M`), and `automatic_shard: true` is set on the step and on `mirror.amd`. No tests change.

## Claims

| Step | Was | Planned shards | AMD mirror: was | AMD planned |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `multi-modal-processor` | 4 fixed | 4 | 4 fixed | 4 |
| `v1-kv-connectors` | 4 fixed | 3 | 4 fixed (inherited) | 2 |
| `lora` | 4 fixed | 3 | 4 fixed (inherited) | 2 |
| `spec-decode-draft-model` | 4 fixed | 3 | 2 fixed | 2 |
| `multi-modal-models-extended-generation-2` (optional) | 4 fixed | 3 | 4 fixed (inherited) | 2 |
| `basic-correctness` | 2 fixed | 2 | 2 fixed (inherited) | 1 (one job) |
| `language-models-tests-extra-standard` | 2 fixed | 2 | 2 fixed (inherited) | 1 (one job) |

- Fixed pytest shards split by test count, so shard lengths vary widely and every shard pays the job startup again. The plan balances shards by measured time and drops shards that aren't needed, with each shard under the 20-minute target.
- Every test runs exactly once across the shards, with the same environment as before.

## Validation

- Planned each step and mirror with ci-infra main's `runtime_shard.plan_step` against this branch and main's timings on the step's own queue.
- Rendered each step and mirror with the pipeline generator and ran every shard's commands against a mock test tree, as a PR build and with main's `pytest -p ci_otel` wrapper. Every test ran in exactly one shard, with the same env. The two mirrors that plan to one shard were confirmed to stay one job.
- Not covered by the mock: `multi-modal-models-extended-generation-2` selects tests with vLLM's dynamic `split(group=0)` marker, which the mock tree doesn't define. It is optional, so a build scoped to it and its mirror checks it on real hardware.
- `/ci run` exercises the other six steps and their mirrors.

## Details

- **Left out, still on fixed shards.**
  - `language-models-tests-hybrid`: each job first builds mamba-ssm and causal-conv1d from source, which every extra shard would repeat. It waits for #58795.
  - `basic-models-tests-extra-initialization`: the plan comes out over budget, with shards over 30 minutes.
  - `multi-modal-processor-cpu`: main has no per-file timings for it.
  - `spec-decode-mtp-other-acceptance-nightly`: the planner estimates a few minutes against about half an hour on main, so its plan can't be trusted yet.
  - `entrypoints-integration-api-server`: its RPC command sets `PYTHONPATH=/vllm-workspace`, which replaces the path the generator adds for the shard plugin, so that command would fail to load the plugin. Appending `$$PYTHONPATH` makes the planner reject the command. This needs a ci-infra change so the plugin stays importable.
  - `lora-tp-distributed`: fails on main, so a PR build can't validate its shards.
  - `distributed-model-tests-2-gpus`, `kernels-b200`, and the MoE Refactor and Humming evals: they pick tests per shard by hand (a `case` script, or a config file per shard), which needs rewriting as plain pytest first.
- **`caplog`.** `v1-kv-connectors` has files that assert on log text. None of them starts an engine, so test order within a shard doesn't affect them.
- **`lora` starts engines with `spawn` (human).** In [95965](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95965), `test_lora_functions.py` failed twice with `CUDA error: initialization error` in a shard where it ran after only CPU tests. CUDA was already initialized in the pytest process in a way `torch.cuda.is_initialized()` misses, so vLLM forked the engine core. On main's fixed shards a GPU kernel test happens to run first and switches vLLM to `spawn`. The step now sets `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`, as other steps do, so the result doesn't depend on shard order; the AMD mirror inherits it.
- **Timeouts unchanged (human).** `timeout_in_minutes` stays per job, as in #61200 and #61477. A single-job fallback (no plan, or the `VLLM_CI_RUNTIME_SHARD` rollback switch) can outrun it. Making the timeout follow the shard count belongs in a central timeout setting.
- **Where to look.** The seven steps in `.buildkite/test_areas/{models_multimodal,misc,lora,spec_decode,basic_correctness,models_language}.yaml`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DCP] Support strided LSE in direct A2A reduction
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Fix the `partial LSE must have packed heads` error when using `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=1` with transposed FlashAttention MLA LSE tensors, as encountered with **DeepSeek-V2-Lite**. The direct P2P kernel now reads both tensor strides, without a contiguous copy. Unlike the NCCL fallback proposed in [#54472](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54472), this enables the direct path for these LSE layouts. ## Claims - Enable direct P2P for strided LSE without changing reduction arithmetic or backend defaults. - Improve DeepSeek-V2-Lite throughput at concurrency 32/128 on the measured long-context workload; c512 is inconclusive. ## Validation ### Serving performance DeepSeek-V2-Lite, **8 x H100 80 GB**, TP=DCP=8, expert parallelism enabled, Q/KV gather through NCCL. Both arms use the same image and Mooncake agentic workload; only `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A` changes between 0 and 1. Metric: **generated output tokens/second/GPU**; higher is better. Three nodes, two order-balanced repetitions per node: six paired measurements per concurrency. | Concurrency | A2A NCCL | A2A direct P2P | Paired throughput gain | 95% CI | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 32 | 343.97 | 359.51 | +4.52% | +2.93% to +6.13% | | 128 | 617.97 | 638.68 | +3.35% | +2.29% to +4.41% | | 512 | 860.21 | 868.15 | +0.92% | -1.47% to +3.36% | At c512, the interval includes small slowdowns and improvements: zero regression is not established. These points vary concurrency, not context length. Performance was measured before rebasing, with the same kernel fix; the newer build was revalidated for correctness, not rebenchmarked.
Benchmark methodology and versions Maximum context 163,840; 60 GiB KV cache/GPU; FlashInfer autotune off; AIperf 0.12.0; fresh server/cold prefix cache; no timed profiling. Request counts: 128/256/1,024; all 16,896 requests succeeded. Trace: `64k_400_90kv_agent_new_noschedule_short_15perc.jsonl`, filtered to input plus output lengths <=163,840. Model revision: `604d5664dddd88a0433dbae533b7fe9472482de0`. Throughput: arithmetic means. Gains: paired log ratios averaged per node, with a t(2) interval over three node means. Output-token totals differ by <=0.147% within pairs. Benchmark upstream base: `f3b77eff640b5ed5cc9221a4f5f402ab65adc021`; patched source: `132c7f5fc41094d91aecb72cd03389326ff80431`.
### Correctness - **Four GPU tests passed, zero skips:** packed/padded/transposed LSE, singleton tokens, empty shards, and graph replay; packed/strided kernel outputs are bitwise-identical for identical inputs. - Latest DeepSeek rerun passed eager TP=2 and graph TP=2/8 numerical/path checks. Traces confirm direct kernels. Packed-copy/strided-P2P model controls produced identical saved outputs. - Additional models are being tested; current model-level evidence covers DeepSeek-V2-Lite only.
Test command and numerical limitations On at least four peer-access-capable H100 GPUs, with the patched build: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/distributed/test_dcp_direct_a2a_lse_reduce.py \ --noconftest -k direct_a2a_matches_reference -v -s ``` `--noconftest` avoids unrelated dependencies. CI is configured for the two-rank cases on two H100s; four-rank cases passed locally. Upstream CI has not run for this branch. Lint, syntax, and `git diff --check` passed. Six prompts, 32 tokens each; comparable logprob bounds: 0.5 maximum / 0.1 per-prompt mean. First divergences require mutual top-five membership and greedy gap <=0.25; later, different contexts are not compared. This is not broad accuracy evaluation or bitwise NCCL/P2P equivalence. One default-scheduling comparison exceeded these bounds; unchanged reruns and fixed-scheduling controls passed. NCCL itself varied across runs, and its rejected output also exceeds the gap bound against packed-copy P2P. The precise cause remains unisolated; tolerances were not relaxed.
## Details FlashAttention MLA's `[heads, tokens]` LSE becomes a strided `[tokens, heads]` view after transpose. Reading both strides fixes addressing without adding copies, allocations, or synchronization. The receive buffer and combine kernel are unchanged. Output-layout/capacity restrictions and oversized-prefill fallback remain. This does **not** fix the separate GLM attention-output layout issue [#54305](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54305). If [#54472](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54472) lands first, relax only its LSE guard for this newly supported layout. Related test-fixture/CI work: [#55492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55492); consolidate overlapping support changes if it lands first. AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, validation. ---

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build] Drop CUDA 12.9 from the release pipeline
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Drop CUDA 12.9 from the release pipeline (`.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml`). CUDA 13.0 is already the default variant, so this stops building and publishing the extra `cu129` wheels and Docker images.

## Claims

- Removes 9 release-pipeline steps:
  - `Build wheel - {x86_64,aarch64} - CUDA 12.9`
  - `Build release image - {x86_64,aarch64} - CUDA 12.9`, and the Ubuntu 24.04 versions of both
  - `Create multi-arch manifest - CUDA 12.9`, and its Ubuntu 24.04 version
  - `Publish nightly multi-arch image to DockerHub - CUDA 12.9`
- Removes the `cuda-12-9` and `cuda-12-9-ubuntu-24-04` targets from `publish-release-images.sh` and from the DockerHub publish matrix.
- Removes the unused `CUDA_ARCH_{X86,AARCH64}_CU129` env vars.
- Nothing is added. The CUDA 13.0, Rubin CUDA 13.4, ROCm, XPU and CPU steps are unchanged.

## Validation

- Compared the step labels in the YAML before and after the change: exactly the 9 CUDA 12.9 steps are gone, no steps were added, and no `depends_on` points at a missing key/id.
- The DockerHub publish matrix is now `cuda-13-0, cuda-13-0-ubuntu-24-04, rocm, rocm72, xpu, cpu`.
- `bash -n` and shellcheck pass on `publish-release-images.sh`, and `pre-commit run` passes on the changed files.
- No release build has been run yet. A release or nightly build of this branch should show no CUDA 12.9 jobs.

## Details

- After the next release, the `vllm/vllm-openai:*-cu129*` DockerHub tags and the `cu129` wheel variant (both nightly and release) will stop getting updates.
- **Follow-up needed:** `setup.py` (`detect_system_cuda_variant`) still maps CUDA 12 torch to the `cu129` precompiled-wheel variant. For CUDA 12 users, `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` will no longer find wheels for new commits. That fix and the install-doc updates (`gpu.cuda.inc.md` still says the default is 12.9) are left out to keep this PR to the pipeline.
- Duplicate check: no open PR removes CUDA 12.9 from the release pipeline. #55387 changes the default CUDA from 13.0 to 13.2 and does not touch cu129.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Keep a per-PR 2-GPU core of the NIXL PD accuracy sweeps
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

#62564 moved the 4-GPU L4 PD-disagg accuracy steps to nightly-only, leaving PRs without NVIDIA-side PD accuracy coverage (the AMD mirrors still run on PRs per #62567). This adds one automatic 2-GPU L4 step that keeps a core set of NIXL PD paths and architectures running on every PR, with prefill and decode sharing GPUs where needed to stay within the 2-GPU budget.

Not a duplicate of #62568, which shards the nightly-only 4-GPU sweeps themselves; this PR restores per-PR coverage at a smaller scale.

## Claims

- A single new automatic step, `(L4) NixlConnector PD accuracy core` (`nixlconnector-pd-accuracy-core-2-gpus`), runs 10 configurations on a 2-GPU L4 pod (~2.5-2.7 GPU-h per PR) covering every model family in the NIXL PD suite that fits a 24 GB L4:

| # | Config | Model | Path / architecture covered | P / D GPUs | Util |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | TP1/TP1 | Qwen3-0.6B | Dense GQA baseline, pull connector | 0 / 1 dedicated | 0.6 |
| 2 | P-TP1 / D-TP2 | Qwen3-0.6B | Hetero-TP, decoder TP>1 | 0 / 1,0 shared | 0.35 |
| 3 | P-TP2 / D-TP1 | Qwen3-0.6B | Hetero-TP, prefiller TP>1 | 0,1 / 0 shared | 0.35 |
| 4 | DP-EP (P-TP1, D-DP2) | deepseek-vl2-tiny | MoE expert parallel + DP-attention decode | 0 / 1,0 shared | 0.4 |
| 5 | Push PP2xTP1 | Qwen3-0.6B | NixlPushConnector, PP prefill layer slicing | 0,1 / 0,1 shared | 0.35 |
| 6 | SLEEP_WAKE TP1/TP1 | Qwen3-0.6B | Sleep/wake round-trip before serving | 0 / 1 dedicated | 0.6 |
| 7 | TP1/TP1 | deepseek-vl2-tiny | MLA KV transfer | 0 / 1 dedicated | 0.8 |
| 8 | TP1/TP1 | granite-4.0-h-tiny | Hybrid SSM Mamba2 conv state (+ small MoE) | 0 / 1 dedicated | 0.8 |
| 9 | TP1/TP1 | Qwen3.5-0.8B | Hybrid SSM GDN conv state | 0 / 1 dedicated | 0.8 |
| 10 | TP1/TP1 | gemma-4-E2B-it | Sliding-window attention + model-native cross-layer KV sharing (`num_kv_shared_layers: 20`) | 0 / 1 dedicated | 0.8 |

- The gemma config was previously unreachable: no CI step ever set `SW_ATTN`, so gemma PD accuracy had no coverage anywhere, including nightly. Sleep/wake previously ran nightly only (inside the 4-GPU step).
- `run_accuracy_test.sh` is unchanged; all engine launch logic is reused. The new sweep script follows the existing `config_sweep_*` pattern.

## Validation

No GPUs were available locally, so validation was static plus the `/ci run` below:

- `pre-commit` hooks pass on the commit (shellcheck with the repo rcfile, Buildkite key check, test tethering).
- Stubbed dry-run of the sweep script executes all 10 configs with the intended env and args (verified by capturing the `run_accuracy_test.sh` invocations).
- GPU-assignment math from `run_accuracy_test.sh` simulated for a 2-GPU pod: shared configs peak at 0.7-0.8 memory fraction per GPU (two engines), dedicated configs at 0.6-0.8. DeepSeek-VL2-Tiny is ~6.5 GB bf16 (3B total / 1B activated), fitting two engines on one 24 GB L4 at 0.4.
- `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` HF config verified to declare `num_kv_shared_layers: 20`, and vLLM consumes that key natively (`add_kv_sharing_layers_to_kv_cache_groups`), so config 10 exercises cross-layer KV sharing without any extra flag.
- First `/ci run nixlconnector-pd-accuracy-core-2-gpus` is the real gate: configs 2-5 (P/D GPU co-location) and 10 (first-ever execution of the gemma PD config) have never run on hardware.

## Details

- Sharing mechanics: `run_accuracy_test.sh` spreads engines modulo the visible GPUs, so on a 2-GPU pod every TP>1 config co-locates prefill and decode ranks. Shared configs cap `--gpu-memory-utilization` at 0.35 (0.4 for vl2-tiny) so two engines fit side by side on 24 GB L4s; Qwen3-0.6B is ~1.2 GB bf16 per TP1 engine.
- Left in the nightly-only 4-GPU sweeps: TP2/TP2, FlashInfer, Mamba1, the wider cross-layer and SW sweeps, MoE DP-EP variants at higher util. Cross-layer layout keeps per-PR coverage via the existing 2-GPU MultiConnector step (normal + BLHNC).
- No AMD mirror on the new step: the MI300/MI355 mirrors of the nightly-only steps are `optional: false` (#62567) and already cover these paths on PRs.
- Known gap left out of scope: the NHD decoder layout (`enable_permute_local_kv`) is not wired to any CI step, nightly included. Worth a separate PR if that path matters.
- Follow-up option: once #62568 lands, this step could enroll in `automatic_shard` to cut wall time across jobs at the same GPU-hour cost.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode on MI300X and MI325X (gfx942)
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR ports the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode kernels of #60397 to gfx942 (MI300X and MI325X). A standard decoder layer then runs as 2 kernels instead of 32. The path is opt-in with `--monokernel`, as on gfx950.

The PR was rebased onto `main` after #61082 as one commit. The commits after it merge `main` and answer the second review (see Details). gfx942 now runs the same layers whole as gfx950, with the switch of #61082 (see Details). The latest commits take the PR out of shared code, as RFC #60904 asks, and merge `main` with #62131 (see Details). The AgentX and GSM8K comparisons below are from 67206b7 and the commits before it, when the switch was `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`. The checks of the latest commits are at the end of Validation.

## Claims

MI325X, TP4, DSpark with 5 drafts. Each AgentX run is 3,600 s and is scored with InferenceX's own result code.

- AgentX at concurrency 1, against `main`: interactivity P50 goes from **216.85 to 503.53 tokens/s/user** (2.32×), P90 from **182.25 to 411.26** (2.26×), and total throughput per GPU from 4,024 to 6,546 tokens/s (1.63×).
- AgentX at concurrency 2, 4 and 8, against InferenceX's published MI325X points: P90 goes from **153.22 to 368.64** (2.41×), from **142.75 to 316.28** (2.22×) and from **81.52 to 162.61** (1.99×).
- A standard decoder layer takes 115 µs instead of 320 µs. A decode period of one request takes 7.2 ms instead of 17.9 ms.
- GSM8K strict match at concurrency 7, 3 runs each: `main` 0.9247 and this PR 0.9270 on average (pooled p 0.49). The difference is not significant.
- On a2ce22d7e317 at concurrency 7, GPQA-Diamond is 85.0%, AIME25 99.0% and RULER NIAH 40 of 40 in every cell, against 85.3%, 99.4% and 40 of 40 for the reference arm of #60397 on MI355X.
- The gfx942 code runs only with `--monokernel`, on gfx942. Outside `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/` and the tests, the PR adds an 8-line hook to the DSpark speculator and two CI jobs.
- On gfx950 all 76 builds of the mono kernels, the 12 of the DSpark draft's runner included, have the same register and LDS use as on `main` and the same count of each instruction, apart from 1 or 2 more `s_waitcnt` in K2 and the FFN launch. The draft runner's scratch is now laid out for its MoE, see Details.
- On MI355X with `--monokernel` at TP2, two runs of each arm on 6caadd0, before #62131: GSM8K strict match 0.9257 and 0.9242 against 0.9249 and 0.9272 for `main` (see Validation).

## Limits on gfx942

- TP4 only. At TP2 the path logs one line and every layer runs vLLM's path.
- Decode steps of up to 42 rows, which is 7 requests with 5 DSpark drafts. A gfx942 workgroup has 64 KB of LDS, against 160 KB on gfx950, so a GEMV pass takes 6 tokens instead of 16. A larger step, prefill, a mixed step and a PIECEWISE graph run vLLM's path on every layer and every rank.
- gfx942 has no scaled FP4 or FP8 MFMA and uses FNUZ FP8, so the kernels read their own copies of the weights. At TP4 the weights take 170.11 GiB a rank instead of 98.88 GiB. On MI325X with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` the KV cache still holds 11.18 million tokens. MI300X (192 GiB) does not fit this well, so the numbers here are for MI325X.

## Details

- **Layers.** gfx942 runs every backbone layer whole, as gfx950 does since #61082. The index layers use vLLM's FP8 indexer, because the MXFP4 indexer cache needs CDNA4. vLLM's compressor and indexer run between K1 and K2, as on gfx950. On gfx942 `mono/keylist.py` then writes the layer's key lists, so K2 is the build without the key table. On gfx942 the 3 DSpark draft layers take the FFN launch after vLLM's attention, built for the draft's 128 experts and top 3, on the target's runner. On gfx950 they run whole on a runner of their own, as #62131 added.
- **gfx942 helper ops** in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/`: the sparse indexer's decode top-512 (`topk512_gfx942.cu`) and its candidate logits, the SWA decode metadata and the top-k packing as one launch each, and DSpark's Markov sampling as one launch a draft step. With `--monokernel` on gfx942 the V4.1 ROCm attention takes the indexer layer of `sparse_indexer.py`. It runs vLLM's ROCm indexer op on every step except a step of only decode rows, which runs the decode path of that op with the top-k launches in front of vLLM's ops. The DSpark speculator asks the draft model's `sample_sequential` first, and the DSv4.1 draft model runs the fused Markov launches there. `draft_lm_head.py` pads the DSpark draft's 5-row logits GEMM to 6 rows, so that vLLM's dispatch takes the torch GEMM instead of `wvSplitK`. For the 32320 × 5120 lm_head shard that takes 96 µs instead of 295 µs on MI325X. Each helper leaves a call it cannot take to vLLM's own op. `topk512_gfx942.cu` is built with hipcc when the model is created. If the build fails, a warning is logged and the indexer runs vLLM's top-k ops.
- **Weight copies.** The routed experts are copied in the byte order of the gfx942 GEMVs, without vLLM's padding columns, and the dense linears as e4m3 bytes, because vLLM dequantizes those to bf16 on gfx942. The copies are made when vLLM processes the weights at load, so vLLM counts them as model memory when it sizes the KV cache. A reload writes the new copies into the first ones in place, because the kernels and the captured CUDA graphs hold their addresses.
- **Changes outside the model directory.** One hook in the DSpark speculator: `_sample_sequential` asks the draft model's `sample_sequential` first, if the model has one, and runs its own loop when the call returns False. Only the DSv4.1 draft model has one, and it takes a step only with `--monokernel` on gfx942. The rest are the two CI jobs. The earlier hooks in `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` are now the indexer layer of `sparse_indexer.py`. The change of the padding loops of `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` is dropped, because #58633 parallelises the same padding.
- **Merge of #62131.** #62131 runs the DSpark draft layers whole on gfx950, on a runner of their own whose MoE takes one FP4 group an ug task (`DRAFT_UG_GROUPS`). Its scratch was laid out for the default two groups, and with one group the ug flags take twice the room. So the flags of the upper half of the tasks were written over the start of the `normed` rows that the MoE reads as its input, at TP 2 and 4 and for every step width. Only the draft layers could be affected, not the target's output, and in a GSM8K check on MI355X `main` accepted as many drafts as this PR, so the overlap did not show there. `scratch_layout` and `scratch_bytes` now take the runner's groups. `run_ffn` checks that each MoE region of a build fits the layout, and that check found the overlap when the draft runner's K2 was built. The FFN launch reads the target's layout, because it runs on the target's runner, also for a gfx942 draft layer.
- **Since the first review.** The branch is rebased onto `main` as one commit. The gfx942 ops moved from `vllm/model_executor/layers/dsv41_gfx942/` into `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/`, as RFC #60904 asks for model kernels. `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_SHADOW` and its layer-by-layer check are removed. The rebase onto #61082 takes its switch and its layer plan on gfx942 too. That removes the gfx942 paths of their own for the first layer, the window layers and the index layers, apart from `mono/keylist.py`.
- **Since the second review.** The kernel tests moved to `tests/kernels/models/amd/`. The fused Markov test checks each draft token against vLLM's `_sample_logits` on the same step's cached logits. The change to vLLM's skinny GEMM dispatch is reverted, and only the DSpark draft's lm_head avoids `wvSplitK`, with `--monokernel` on gfx942. `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` and a gfx942 graph replay test in `test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` run at TP4 in a new four-GPU MI300 job. On gfx942 the first layer's output bound in `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` is 6% instead of 3%, because vLLM's gfx942 MoE keeps bf16 activations and the kernels quantize them to MXFP8, which alone moves the FFN output of the test's random weights by 4.65%. The residual stream then differs by up to 2.5% instead of 0.4 to 0.7%, so past the first layer a routing near-tie there is a gap of up to 0.02 instead of 0.01, and up to a third of the tokens may flip an expert instead of a quarter (22% seen).
- **Relation to other PRs.** Draft #61482 moves the FlyDSL stages to `vllm/models/common/amd/mono/`, and this PR edits the files it moves. Whichever of the two merges second needs a rebase. If this PR merges first, its gfx942 tests can check #61482's move on MI325X. #62131 is merged into this branch, see Merge of #62131. #58633 parallelises the padding of `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`, which this PR changed until the latest commits, and neither PR needs the other. #61311 moves `amd/mono/` to `amd/specialized_decode/mono/` and replaces `mono_decode.py`, as RFC #60904 describes. A trial merge of the two conflicts in 15 files, among them `mono_decode.py` and `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`, which #61311 deletes and this PR changes. So whichever of the two merges second needs a port. #61869 adds a fused Markov sampler at the start of `_sample_sequential`, next to this PR's hook, and the two merge there without a conflict.
- **Follow-ups.** Steps of more than 42 rows on gfx942, so that 8 or more concurrent requests with 5 drafts also take the mono path. One copy of the routed experts instead of two. Other TP sizes on gfx942. The whole DSpark draft layers on gfx942, as on gfx950. `topk512_gfx942.cu` as a compiled op in `csrc/`.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #60623. Ports the vLLM code for 6 more models to the upstream Transformers 5.16.1 schemas, and deletes their vendored configs and processors (9 files). Also fixes registry entries that kept models out of CI.

Related PRs:
- **#61392:** the DeepSeek-V4 part of this PR, split out.
- **#61813:** the MiniMax-M3 part of this PR, split out.
- **#61883:** the Inkling part of this PR, split out.
- **#47438:** a stale draft (last updated 2026-07-16) with a partial OpenCUA fix. This PR supersedes it.

## Claims

- Deletes the vendored configs for `step3p5`, `muse_glimmer`, `cosmos3_edge`, `colpali`, `colmodernvbert` and `qianfan_ocr`. It also deletes the vendored `cosmos3_edge` and `muse_glimmer` processors, and the model code now reads the upstream fields:
  - **Step3p5:** reads `layer_types` / `mlp_layer_types` / per-type `rope_parameters`. Upstream `Step3p7TextConfig` is registered in `_CONFIG_REGISTRY`, because the hub remote code fails validation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][NIXL] Shard a GQA draft's KV by head under an MLA target
commits.pr_body:
## Update (2026-10-13)

Adopted @NickLucche's simplification from #60368 (thanks!): the source files now match that branch exactly, carried as a commit authored by him (his three commits squashed, his sign-off kept), followed by one commit of mine adapting the tests. Relative to the earlier revision:
- draft-region identity is computed once at `register_kv_caches` into `_head_sharded_draft_regions` (via `_layer_specs`), replacing the per-region head-count list and the three per-call helpers;
- the push-mode guard lives in `NixlPushConnectorWorker` and rejects only heterogeneous TP, so equal-TP push works; the base class keeps the `tp_ratio < 0` / DCP rejection;
- `tp_mapping.compute_head_offset` carries the rank-offset arithmetic for both the target and the draft mapping.
Tests were adapted to the new structure (see Test Plan); the end-to-end results below predate this revision and were obtained with the earlier implementation of the same behaviour.

## Purpose

Fixes #58470.

NIXL P/D mis-handles a draft model's KV when **all three** hold:

1. **The target is MLA** (e.g. GLM-5.3), so NIXL maps every KV region as replicated: `total_num_kv_heads=1`, `rank_offset_factor=0`.
2. **The draft is not MLA** (e.g. DFlash2, 8 KV heads), so its KV is actually split by head across TP.
3. **Prefill TP ≠ decode TP** (e.g. a DEP8 prefill with attention TP1 feeding a TP8 decoder), so each decode rank needs a different head slice.

Drop any one and it works: an MLA draft (MTP), or equal P/D TP. `_is_region_replicated` already marks the draft regions SPLIT, but three places still use the model-wide MLA answer:

| where | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| handshake size check (`model_replicated = self.use_mla or …`) | rejects the correct geometry, accepts an unscaled draft block | checks draft regions as SPLIT |
| read offset (`_build_fa_remote`) | every decode rank reads draft head 0 | rank *r* reads head *r* |
| hetero-TP layout guard | skipped when `use_mla` | requires the same block-contiguous layout on P and D |

**Fix.** When the target is MLA and the draft isn't, build a second `TPMapping` from the draft's KV head count (`compute_tp_mapping(..., head_sharded_kv_heads=...)`). The draft's SPLIT regions use it for reads, size checks and the layout guard; MLA regions are unchanged. Prefill TP > decode TP and DCP are rejected with `NotImplementedError` for such drafts. Mamba, CSA-linear and MLA drafts behave as before.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR touches this. Related:
- #49230 (merged): checks that P and D speculative configs match; they do here.
- #54926: Gemma 4 MTP draft groups are not transferred at all.
- #57309: moves helpers out of `tp_mapping.py`; a refactor only.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_tp_mapping.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py
```

New tests:
- `test_resolve_head_sharded_draft_kv_heads`
- `test_head_sharded_draft_under_mla_target_gets_gqa_offset`
- `test_handshake_mla_target_reads_draft_head_slice` (also `_block_outermost`, for BLHNC)
- `test_handshake_mla_target_rejects_unsharded_draft_block`
- `test_handshake_mla_target_rejects_draft_with_prefill_tp_above_decode`
- `test_head_sharded_draft_regions_check_layer_identity`
- `test_head_sharded_draft_push_rejects_heterogeneous_tp` (push worker)

End-to-end A/B on 2 × 8×H200 over NIXL/IB:
- **Model:** GLM-5.3 FP8 + DFlash2 (k=4).
- **Topology:** P DP8/EP8 (attention TP1) → D TP8, `LBHNC`.
- **Builds:** the same wheel (`0.30.1rc1.dev29+g711fc55c1`) with and without this change.
- **Workload:** 80 MT-Bench prompts, 256 tokens, temperature 0, following `nixl_integration/test_spec_decode_acceptance.py`.
- **Comparison:** each prompt goes once through the P/D proxy and once straight to decode (local prefill), both on the same decode server.

## Test Result

**Unit:**

- The 2 failures are `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller`, which needs 24 GiB of RAM; it fails on `main` too.
- The new tests fail on `main`.

| this PR | **80 / 80**, acceptance length **3.221**, 0 failed transfers | 80 / 80, acceptance length 3.253 |

- **Acceptance:** P/D is within 1.0% of local prefill. The upstream test's tolerance is 5%.
- **Local path:** the local-prefill counters are identical on both builds.

**Follow-up B300 validation (GLM-5.3 NVFP4 + DFlash2):**

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][AuxOutput] Send routed-experts block hashes only for computed or scheduled blocks
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Split from #62044 (by @faresobeid): only the scheduler-side hash fix. The store eviction fix is #62392.

The scheduler sent a request's block hashes to the worker as soon as they existed. A prompt's hashes all exist before its first chunk runs, so with chunked prefill the worker pinned one store object for every prompt block, including blocks whose KV had not been computed yet. When those objects were still stored from an earlier turn, the extra pins could push the KV-sized store over capacity and make `put()` raise `BlockObjectStoreError` in the writer thread.

`AuxOutputSchedulerConnector` now sends only the hashes of blocks covered by `num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled_tokens` (or `num_computed_tokens` for hash-only updates and finished requests). It takes the hash block size from the scheduler to do that.

As a side effect, when a request finishes and its last sampled token completes a block, that block's hash is no longer sent unless a step that computes that token is already in flight: otherwise the token's KV is never computed, so the worker held a reference to a key with no stored object.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/distributed/aux_output_connector
```

- `test_routed_experts_hashes_follow_scheduled_tokens` runs a 160-token prompt with a 64-token budget and 20 decode steps through the real scheduler, and checks the number of hashes sent after each step against fixed values: 4, 8 and 10 during prefill, then 11 once the decode tokens complete the next block.
- `test_scheduler_connector_sends_only_computed_hashes_off_schedule` (hash-only update, finish) schedules a request's first 4-token block, then lets a settled token complete a second hash block while only 7 tokens are computed. Neither a hash-only update nor the terminal event may send the second hash; the hash-only update sends it once the eighth token is computed.
- `test_worker_does_not_pin_unscheduled_prompt_blocks` drives the scheduler connector and the worker with a 4-object store. A first request stores 4 prompt blocks and finishes. A second request with the same prompt runs its first 4-token chunk next to a request that stores a new block.

## Test Result

- With this change: the new tests pass; `test_scheduler.py` and `tests/distributed/aux_output_connector` pass (288 tests).
- On `main`, with the new constructor argument removed from the tests, all new tests fail:
  - the scheduler sends all 10 prompt hashes at the first step (`[10, 10, ...] != [4, 8, ...]`);
  - after the first block is sent, the hash-only update and the terminal event both send the second hash although only 7 of its 8 tokens are computed;
  - the worker pins all 4 stored prompt blocks, so storing the new block raises `BlockObjectStoreError: auxiliary output store cannot retain the requested batch: limit=4 objects`, the writer-thread failure seen in production.
- Reverting only one of the three bounds to "send every hash" fails only the tests for that path: the scheduled-step bound fails the scheduler and worker tests, and the hash-only and terminal-event bounds each fail their case of `test_scheduler_connector_sends_only_computed_hashes_off_schedule`. The scheduler test cannot see the terminal-event bound, because its request finishes with 179 computed tokens and 11 complete hash blocks either way.

## Purpose

`vllm-bench` has no Responses API backend, so this fails on main:

```text
$ VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1 vllm bench serve --backend openai-responses --endpoint /v1/responses ...
error: invalid value 'openai-responses' for '--backend <BACKEND>'
```

This ports the Python `openai-responses` backend from #54628. Reasoning deltas count toward TTFT and ITL, latency ends at the last token event, and a stream that ends without `response.completed` or `response.incomplete` fails the request. Without `--endpoint` it uses `/v1/responses`, the way the other Rust backends pick their endpoint.

Chunks are not trimmed like in the chat and completions backends, because a chunk can end between an event's `event:` and `data:` lines.

## Purpose

When a target FULL CUDA graph pads its request count, `DPSyncState.num_reqs` describes graph capacity rather than the number of scheduled requests. Reusing that capacity for uniform drafter steps makes active DP ranks select larger draft graphs than needed.

This PR keeps the DP-wide maximum real request count alongside graph capacity and uses it for uniform drafter dispatch. ## Overview

## Claims

- Catches the CVE-2026-27893 pattern at the exact vulnerable lines, and the later reintroduction in #37408.
- Zero findings on current `main`, so it adds no churn.
- Not a duplicate: no open or closed PRs add a check for this pattern. #18018 added the pickle-import ban and mentioned broader security checks as a possible follow-up.

- `pytest tests/tools/test_check_trust_remote_code.py`: 14 passed

| Code | Result |
|---|---|
| `nemotron_vl.py` / `kimi_k25.py` before #36192 (`git show 00bd08e^:…`) | flags lines 459 and 177, the two CVE lines |
| Same files after #36192 | clean |
| `quark.py` at the head of #37408 | flags line 96, the reintroduced pattern |

## Details

- **Why:** the pattern keeps coming back. CVE-2026-27893 was itself the pattern surviving two earlier fixes (CVE-2025-66448, CVE-2026-22807) in different code paths, and #37408 reintroduced it 12 days after the fix. Review caught that one; this catches it in CI first.
- **AST-based**, like `check_boolean_context_manager.py`, so docstrings, strings and comments never trigger it.
- **Only a literal `True` passed in a call** is flagged. `model_config.trust_remote_code`, `False`, and default values in function signatures are fine.

- **Escape hatch:** `# trust-remote-code: ok (reason)` on the same line.
- **Limitation (intentional):** it targets accidental reintroduction, not deliberate evasion (e.g. `x = True; f(trust_remote_code=x)`). That's the job of review.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][V1] Null sliding-window block-table entries below the window
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #60560.

The sliding-window KV manager frees blocks once they fall wholly outside a request's window, but the worker's persistent block table keeps the freed block ids. Attention kernels load KV in tiles (FA4 uses 128-key tiles on SM100). With 64-token pages, the tile that holds the window start can include one page lying wholly below the window. That page is masked, but masked NaN still propagates (0 × NaN). After the freed block is reused, its bytes can decode as NaN in the layer that reads it, and that request's attention output turns NaN.

#60560 has the full analysis. In short, on B300 with a DFlash2 drafter (all 6 layers sliding window, 2048) under the hybrid KV cache manager and `--block-size 64`:
- draft acceptance falls from about 40% to 27–29% at 32 concurrent sessions;
- the first divergence is NaN in the last draft layer's attention;
- about 21% of that layer's in-tile stale pages contain fp8 NaN bytes.

This PR makes the worker never hand those entries to attention. When `gather_block_tables` builds the forward-pass tables, every sliding-window entry wholly below `first_scheduled_position - (sliding_window - 1 + extra_retained_tokens)` is replaced by the null block:
- **No query of the step can attend those positions.**
- **The cutoff is never below the manager's free boundary.** The manager frees on the processed-token count, which is at most the first scheduled position, so every block it may have freed is covered.
- **Only the forward-pass copy changes.** Slot mappings and the persistent tables are untouched.
- **GPU only.** The first scheduled position is the request's `num_computed_tokens`, already on the device, so there is no host sync.
- **Every sliding-window spec is covered.** `SlidingWindowSpec.num_retained_tokens` gives the reach. (`KpoolTailSpec`, which an earlier revision opted out, was removed on `main` in #57169; its successor `CircularBufferSpec` is not a `SlidingWindowSpec` and is unaffected.)
- **Context parallelism is excluded.** Masking is disabled when `cp_size > 1`, where a block-table column is not a contiguous token range.

Speculator steps that reuse the gathered tables (e.g. DFlash) are covered too, since their queries sit at or after the target's first scheduled position.

### Scope

The change is not specific to any model or drafter. It applies to every KV cache group whose spec is a `SlidingWindowSpec` (including `SlidingWindowMLASpec`), target or draft, with any attention backend. Why it is safe:
- **No KV write is redirected.** Every KV write slot is computed from the persistent tables (`compute_slot_mappings`), or, for DFlash, from this step's positions, which are above the cutoff.
- **Entries are whole KV blocks.** Since #57169 `BlockTables` holds one entry per KV block, so the cutoff is `max(first_pos - reach, 0) // block_size` entries.

Not covered:
- **The V1 model runner.** The default V2 runner is covered; V1 is still selected for some speculators, DBO and some ROCm architectures.
- **Context parallelism (DCP/PCP).** Excluded on purpose, since a block-table column is not a contiguous token range there.
- **Chunked-local attention.** Not changed. Its chunk boundaries are multiples of the KV tile, so no wholly-outside page shares a tile.

**Assumption:** the null block holds no NaN. The KV cache is zero-allocated, and the null entries the tables already contain (sliding-window prefix hits, P/D tail clipping) rely on the same thing.

**Validation:** end-to-end validation so far covers a DFlash2 drafter under the hybrid KV cache manager. A check on a target model with sliding-window layers (e.g. gpt-oss, Gemma 3) at high concurrency is still to do.

### Relation to existing PRs

- **#42276** (for #42273, "SWA eviction leaves stale block table entries") targets the same stale entries from the scheduler side: it resends the full rewritten block table to the worker after an eviction. It has had merge conflicts since May and no review. This PR is a worker-only alternative: no scheduler or `SchedulerOutput` change, and no table resend. If maintainers prefer #42276's direction, I'm happy to close this one in its favour, and the regression test here should carry over.
- **#53628** fixes the same NaN symptom inside the ROCm prefix-prefill kernel, by masking block-table loads. That is complementary kernel hardening; this PR keeps freed blocks out of every backend's tables.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py`: the new `test_gather_block_tables_nulls_blocks_below_sliding_window` checks:
  - the exact cutoff, including a request with no scheduled tokens;
  - that full-attention groups are untouched;
  - padded rows;
  - that the persistent tables are left unchanged;
  - that rows are copied verbatim when no positions are passed.
- End-to-end on 2× B300, GLM-5.3 NVFP4 + DFlash2, prefill DEP8 / decode 2× TP4 over NIXL, `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC`, `--block-size 64`, hybrid KV cache manager on, decode prefix caching off. Agentic multi-turn traffic (AgentX), 32 concurrent sessions, 900 s. Acceptance = accepted / drafted tokens over the profiling window.
- `pre-commit run ruff-check` and `pre-commit run mypy` on the changed files.

## Test Result

- Unit tests: 11 passed on B300 (the new test and the 10 existing tests in the file).
- Rebased 2026-10-13 onto `main` `791f92135a` (#57169 removed `KpoolTailSpec` and kernel block sizes; the two review suggestions from @TheEpicDolphin are in): 16 passed, 0 failed on B300 (2026-10-14; `test_gpu_block_table.py` incl. the new test, plus the selected `test_kv_cache_utils` cases).
- ruff and mypy: passed.
- End-to-end, same build and traffic:

| | draft acceptance |
|---|---:|
| without this PR | 28.95% |
| **with this PR** | **41.21%** (819,107 / 1,987,756) |
| reference: hybrid KV cache manager off | 39.61% |

The end-to-end run used this exact diff on our serving build (vLLM 0.30.1-based), where it applies unchanged, because that stack (NVFP4 KV, NIXL whole-row registration) is not on `main` yet.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DeepSeek V4.1] Inject Engram at pipeline stage entry
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1 applies trained Engram modules at configured transformer layers. If a pipeline partition starts a non-initial stage on one of those layers, the stage-entry control-flow branch calls mHC pre directly and bypasses the normal Engram branch. Certain valid PP partitions can therefore silently skip an Engram operation for every request. The real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash configuration triggers this at layer 14 with `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=14,26`.

This PR restores the missing NVIDIA operation by applying the local stage-entry Engram after receiving the previous stage's completed residual stream and before mHC pre.

**AMD is affected by the same issue. We currently only have access to NVIDIA hardware, so this PR fixes only the NVIDIA implementation for now.**

## Claims

- Restore Engram when its layer is the first layer of a non-initial pipeline stage.
- Preserve the incoming `pre_mix`, selected Engram hash column, mask, and existing no-hash behavior.
- Add a non-identity regression test to the NVIDIA model CI job.

## Validation

### Environment

- Hardware: two 8 x NVIDIA H20 96GB nodes.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-49cb2bbf71cfd36ee5aa33d1e184b1cddff55294`.

### vLLM launch

Both arms used identical arguments:

```bash
VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=14,26 \
VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1 \
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 18001 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --moe-backend humming \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-async-scheduling
```

### Verify Engram execution at the pipeline boundary

This check verifies that layer 14 executes its trained Engram module before mHC pre when it is the first layer of a pipeline stage.

We compared three configurations using the real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint:

- **Without this PR, PP=1:** the reference configuration. Layer 14 runs within the same pipeline stage as the preceding layers.
- **Without this PR, PP=2 (`14,26`):** the configuration that exposes the bug. The first stage contains 14 layers, so the second stage starts at layer 14.
- **With this PR, PP=2 (`14,26`):** the same pipeline partition with the fix applied, tested independently on both H20 nodes.

Each configuration received the same fixed 256-token prompt and generated two tokens, each constrained to a single allowed token ID. This kept the token sequence fixed across configurations. Each configuration was run twice in eager mode.

#### Was layer 14's Engram actually executed?

| Configuration | Layer 14 Engram executed? | Input passed to layer 14's mHC pre |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Without this PR, PP=1 — reference | Yes | Engram output |
| Without this PR, PP=2 (`14,26`) | **No** | Tensor received from the previous stage, without applying Engram |
| With this PR, PP=2 (`14,26`) — both nodes | **Yes** | Engram output |

The unpatched PP=2 configuration had valid Engram hashes and masks available at layer 14, but never called its Engram module. The missing operation was therefore caused by the stage-entry control flow.

#### Did mHC receive the correct tensor?

We recorded SHA-256 checksums of the full tensors at the pipeline handoff, Engram input/output, and mHC pre input. These checksums track tensor contents; they are separate from the token hashes used by Engram.

For every TP rank, measured step, and repeat, the checks confirmed these paths:

- **Without this PR, PP=2:** the tensor sent by the previous stage was passed directly to mHC pre. Engram was skipped.
- **With this PR, PP=2:** the received tensor was passed to Engram, and Engram's output was passed to mHC pre.
- **PP=1 reference:** Engram's output was also passed to mHC pre.

These comparisons verify the data flow within each run; they do not require bitwise-identical outputs between PP=1 and PP=2.

#### Did Engram make a measurable change?

For runs that executed Engram, we measured the difference between its input and output at layer 14:

| Step | RMS of the Engram update | Tensor elements whose stored values changed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill | 0.03445–0.03557 | 67.22%–67.82% |
| Decode | 0.05899–0.06505 | 81.83%–83.14% |

The update RMS is `RMS(Engram output − Engram input)`. These nonzero differences confirm that skipping this trained Engram module changes the tensor passed to mHC pre.

**This check confirms that the affected PP partition skips a trained Engram operation and that this PR restores it before mHC pre on both tested nodes.** It does not establish an accuracy improvement: captured logits varied across repeated runs and nodes by an amount comparable to the patch effect. The GSM8K results below report the separate end-to-end accuracy evaluation.

### Full GSM8K comparison

Both configurations used PP=2 (`14,26`) with identical evaluation settings: 4-shot, temperature 0, seed 42, and a maximum of 8,192 output tokens.

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://<node-ip>:18001/v1 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --model-id deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-hub modelscope \
  --dataset-args '{"gsm8k":{"few_shot_num":4}}' \
  --seed 42 \
  --eval-batch-size 64 \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0,"max_tokens":8192,"reasoning_effort":"high","seed":42,"timeout":10000}' \
  --timeout 10000 \
  --no-timestamp
```

| Configuration | Correct / Total | Accuracy | API errors | Pod restarts |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Without this PR | 1283 / 1319 | 97.27% | 0 | 0 |
| With this PR | 1283 / 1319 | 97.27% | 0 | 0 |

Seven questions were correct only without the patch, and seven only with it; aggregate accuracy was unchanged.

**We have not observed an end-to-end accuracy loss in this GSM8K evaluation. However, the confirmed omission of a trained Engram operation remains a correctness bug with potential model-quality impact that this benchmark has not demonstrated.**

The focused regression test and full pre-commit suite also passed.

## Details

At the end of a pipeline stage, the previous rank completes its final mHC post and sends the full 3-D residual stream together with `pre_mix`. The next stage starts with `residual=None`, assigns that received stream to `residual`, and calls mHC pre directly. Because normal Engram injection lives in the following `elif`, an Engram on the stage's first layer is silently skipped.

This change injects the local Engram after accepting the completed stream and before mHC pre. It does not repeat the previous stage's post or alter first-layer embeddings, in-stage Engram execution, or batches without Engram hashes.

The real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash configuration has Engram layers 1 and 14. A pipeline partition beginning its second stage at layer 14 can therefore reach this path. Open PR searches for the same Engram pipeline-stage fix found no direct duplicate; related PCP work such as #62183 does not implement this injection.

AI assistance was used for implementation support and a read-only Codex CLI review. Human line-by-line review is still required before requesting maintainer review.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Unit Test] Patch MoE layer unit tests for Blackwell and Rubin
commits.pr_body:
## Overview


Why the buffer grouping is necessary

  The test runs multiple MoE configurations within the same distributed workers. NIXL retains a process-wide communication buffer whose expert capacity is established during its first initialization.

  In the failing sequence, the first configuration allocates capacity for eight experts. Later configurations request 64 experts, but receive the same buffer. NIXL then rejects the request with its active/maximum expert-bound assertion. Running the affected configurations in fresh processes removes that assertion.

  Calling the manager’s destroy() between configurations does not resolve this: it intentionally retains the buffer to support elastic expert-parallel scaling.

  Why rename _group_deepep_ll_configs

  The existing helper already implements the required pattern: group compatible configurations and launch separate workers for incompatible groups. Its purpose now applies to both ROCm DeepEP low-latency and NIXL EP.

  Renaming it to _group_configs_by_buffer_requirements describes that shared responsibility and avoids maintaining two implementations of the same grouping logic. The key includes:

  • Routed hidden size.
  • Expert-parallel size.
  • Total expert count.

  For latent MoE, the routed hidden size is k // 2, so grouping must account for the input transform. Token capacity and the other allocation settings are fixed within the outer test case.

  Fresh workers provide a clear lifetime boundary without changing production buffer management or its elastic-scaling behavior. Grouping also retains buffer reuse among compatible cases: this matrix needs four worker groups, rather than restarting workers for every one of its 52 subcases.

  Why preserve padded weights

  The latent configurations generate 1024-wide expert weights, while NIXL requires a supported hidden size of at least 2048. The layer correctly allocates padded parameters, but the test replaces them with smaller tensors. Activations remain padded, producing:

  Hidden size mismatch 2048 != 1024

  The patch keeps the allocated parameter, zeros its padding, and copies the original weights into the valid hidden-dimension slice. This preserves W13’s input padding and W2’s output padding. Other dimension mismatches still fail an assertion.

  Both corrections belong in the test setup: one respects the communication buffer’s lifetime, and the other respects the layer’s allocated weight layout.

  Related work, PR #61156 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61156), limits NIXL dispatch token capacity. It addresses a different dimension of buffer sizing and does not fix these test weight-loading or cross-configuration lifetime problems.

## Validation



Executed the exact original case:

  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
    'tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py::test_moe_layer[False-nixl_ep-2-1-True]'

| Configuration.  |  passed   |  failed  |
| --------------- | ----------------- | --------------- |
| Original test.     |             24             |        28               |
| Patched test     |             52             |         0                |

Validation used two SM107 and SM100 GPUs with the Oct16 nightly container, NIXL 1.5.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2, and PyTorch 2.16.0.dev20261009+cu134.

Additional worker launches increase test setup overhead and change random draw sequences. This validates the same configuration matrix with unchanged numerical checks; it is not an identical-tensor replay.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Enable PDL for fused MoE top-k gating
commits.pr_body:
## Overview The FP32 router GEMM supports programmatic dependent launch (PDL), but fused MoE `topkGating` uses an ordinary launch. Enable PDL for the consumer on SM90+ with CUDA 12+, allowing it to start early and wait before reading producer-dependent data. ## Claims - On GB200, the M=4 MiniMax-M3 router-to-gating CUDA Graph chain saves **0.486 us (-9.12%)** with hot weights and **0.466 us (-7.77%)** with rotating weights. - In ordinary MiniMax-M3 aggregated serving, mean TPOT improves **0.61–1.16%** at request concurrency 1/16/32. All three paired runs improve for both tested input lengths at these concurrencies. C4 is effectively unchanged. - Pure-prefill C16/C32 mean TTFT regresses **0.54%/0.49%**. The results support a modest decode benefit on this setup; broader workload and platform coverage remains open. ## Validation **End-to-end accuracy (`713192bab`):** Full GSM8K (1,319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, concurrency 8), MiniMax-M3 NVFP4, TP8 on the same 8x GB200 GPUs, with real EAGLE3 verification and three draft tokens. Each variant ran twice without restarting its server. | Strict-match accuracy | Baseline | PDL | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Run 1 | 1247/1319 (94.54%) | 1248/1319 (94.62%) | | Run 2 | 1254/1319 (95.07%) | 1249/1319 (94.69%) | | Mean | 94.81% | 94.66% | Mean change is -0.152 percentage points; baseline repeats differ by 0.531 points. These two repeats per variant do not establish accuracy equivalence. All evaluation requests succeeded. Baseline uses official vLLM v0.29.0; the candidate overlays the pinned PR kernel in the same image, rather than a full PR checkout build. **Serving:** MiniMax-M3 NVFP4, 8x GB200 on two four-GPU nodes, TP8 with expert parallelism disabled, one aggregated worker, FP8 KV/indexer cache, FlashInfer/TRTLLM attention, no prefix caching or speculative decoding. Direct `vllm serve` / `vllm bench serve` uses the same physical GPUs for A/B, three valid pairs per workload, and 64 measured requests per variant per pair. | Request concurrency | TPOT change, ISL/OSL 128/1024 | TPOT change, 8192/1024 | TTFT change, 8192/1 | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | -0.61% | -0.63% | +0.89% | | 4 | +0.05% | -0.01% | -0.12% | | 16 | -1.16% | -1.00% | +0.54% | | 32 | -0.93% | -1.09% | +0.49% | Negative latency changes are better. Changes are computed within each pair and then averaged. For 128/1024 C1, mean TPOT is 3.874 → 3.851 ms; individual paired changes range from -0.82% to -0.48%. These finite bursts and three repeats do not establish statistical significance or sustained-load capacity. **Kernel chain:** M=4, H=6144, E=128, top-4 sigmoid; three same-GPU A/B pairs. Hot-weight latency is 5.330 → 4.844 us. Rotating weights use 64 distinct 3 MiB matrices; paired changes range from -8.28% to -6.51%. Each repetition ends with a non-PDL serial boundary to prevent overlap into the next repetition and premature logits-buffer reuse. Its approximately 0.682 us cost is included equally. Latencies are medians across rounds; savings are medians of paired differences. Isolated gating with that boundary saves 0.076 us (-2.16%). **Correctness and integration:** - 866 unchanged upstream fused-top-k and FP32-router tests passed against the pinned runtime with the PDL overlay. - 360 representative original-versus-patched operator cases per process match with zero tolerance: FP32/FP16/BF16, expert counts 6–512, selected index types/top-k values, bias, normalization, padding, ties and nonfinite values. Equal NaNs are accepted; NaN payload-bit identity is not asserted. - 1,200 preallocated-chain and 960 runtime-dispatch changing-input graph checks passed, including poisoned intermediates and the M=32/33 dispatch boundary. - The changed SM100a CUDA translation unit compiled; the original standalone harness passed Compute Sanitizer memcheck with zero errors. - All 74 raw serving measurements completed: 4,736 requests, zero failures. One JIT-contaminated pair is excluded and replaced as described below. - Separate untimed GPU traces confirm PDL gating on all eight TP ranks. Directly adjacent router/gating calls overlap in residence in 6,720/6,720 patched pairs versus 0/6,720 baseline pairs. Residence includes dependency waits; it does not directly measure time saved.
Runtime pins, commands and measurement controls The serving, kernel-chain and correctness/integration results above use vLLM `9ea8f3ffc354901b740f0b31988900897b7221d7`, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 and CUDA 13.0. Those measurements used the PR CUDA file on base `d2125ea681784c17251c47939f5ed6d1c67384f8`, before the later guard simplifications. Both controls load identically recompiled original/patched translation units, with library hashes verified on every TP rank. This is not a full current-main rebuild. The upstream tests were copied unchanged from the PR base into that pinned runtime. Equivalent in-checkout commands: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fp32_router_gemm.py -v ``` Example client command; sweep the listed length pairs and C=1/4/16/32: ```bash vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \ --model nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 \ --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 64 --num-warmups 8 \ --ignore-eos --seed 1729 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \ --metric-percentiles 50,90,95,99 --save-result --save-detailed ``` Server limits: model length 16384, batched tokens 16384, sequences 32, CUDA Graph capture limit 64, block size 128 and GPU memory utilization 0.9. FlashInfer autotuning and `float32_matmul_precision=high` are enabled. Each variant starts fresh workers and autotuning. Paired variants use the same seed and workload order; the main sequence is A/B, B/A, A/B. Round 0 used eight warmups and exposed attention JIT during measured 8192/1024 C32 requests. That whole pair is excluded. Later pairs use `max(8, 2*C)` warmups; a dedicated same-GPU A/B with verbose JIT monitoring replaces the excluded pair. Neither replacement measurement has observed measured-window JIT. Raw excluded results are retained; each workload has three valid pairs. Capture, JIT/warmup, correctness checks and diagnostic traces are outside timing. Request-level P99 has only 64 samples per run and is descriptive. Eager host-wall results are retained separately from graph GPU timings. The microbench and overlay harnesses are external to this 30-line CUDA diff. ## Details The dependency wait and completion signal precede dependent reads and row-dependent exits. CUDA launches set the PDL attribute without a host architecture query, matching `topk_softplus_sqrt` and `per_token_group_quant`, and check `cudaLaunchKernelEx` errors. Device-side PDL instructions remain guarded by `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900`. Routing math, launch geometry, output layout and the operator API are unchanged. ROCm and the unfused fallback retain their existing paths. Hopper, ROCm and a full current-main build remain unvalidated. For the host-launch cleanup in `09647c0364`, `git diff --check` and `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/topk_softmax_kernels.cu` passed. GPU tests were not rerun for this cleanup; the accuracy results above remain pinned to `713192bab`. OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, validation and this description. The submitting author has reviewed the change and approved this draft submission with the validation scope and limitations documented above. ---

- Adds a `weight_dtype` field to `TestMoEQuantConfig`/`Config` (mirrors `FusedMoEQuantConfig.make()`'s own `(quant_dtype, weight_dtype)` split) to represent the asymmetric W4A16 case (mxfp4 weight, unquantized activation) alongside the symmetric W4A4 case.

- Moves `_interleave_gate_up_rows()` out of `test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` into the shared `tests/kernels/moe/utils.py` helper module.

Three gaps were found while validating on MI350/gfx950 hardware and are scoped around rather than fixed here:
- W4A16's heuristic-dispatch kernel only has a `SWIGLUOAI` specialization, not SILU/GELU, despite `AiterExperts._supports_activation()` declaring broader support (https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2419).
- W4A16 hits the same `topk=1` + `apply_router_weight_on_input` GPU-hang gap as AITER's existing block-scaled FP8 path (https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/2418), just not representable via `config.quant_block_shape` since mxfp4 has no block-shape field.
- W4A16+`SWIGLUOAI` silently computes the wrong thing for bias-free SwiGLU-OAI (~55% sign agreement, ~5x-small magnitude on hardware) instead of raising; only smoke-tested (shape/finite) here until the fix in #59766 lands.

Validated on an MI350/gfx950 host (MXFP4 is unsupported on MI300/gfx942):
- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py::test_modular_kernel_combinations_singlegpu -k mxfp4` — both new W4A16 and W4A4 cases pass (note: `AiterExperts` was split into per-scheme subclasses in #60322, so the original `-k "AiterExperts and mxfp4"` filter no longer matches any test id; use `-k mxfp4`)

commits.pr_body:
## The failure

`(MI300) Model Executor` in [AMD CI 14934](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14934), the only failure among 1238 passing tests:

```
FAILED model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_cache.py::test_ipc_cache_cold_start_and_warm_restart_tp2_ep - TypeError: cannot pickle '_Local' object
```

## The cause

[#55490](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55490) added `test_ipc_cache_cold_start_and_warm_restart_tp2_ep`, which combines `@create_new_process_for_each_test()` with the `capfd` fixture. The wrapper cloudpickles its arguments into the child process and `CaptureFixture` holds a thread-local, so the test raises before it runs. It is the only test in the file with that combination, and the failure is deterministic: the pickle happens before any GPU work.

## The change

The test no longer requests `capfd`. `DSV2_EP_CASE` leaves `check_flashinfer_cache` off and every use of `capfd` in `run_cold_start_and_warm_restart` sits behind that flag, so the fixture was requested but never read. It could not have worked in the child either, which inherits the parent's descriptors. The helper keeps it as an optional parameter, so the in-process cases retain their autotune-cache assertions.

A wider fix, dropping unpicklable fixtures inside the wrapper in `tests/utils.py`, would silently change behaviour for other tests, so this stays local to the one test that is wrong.

## Tests

`test_ipc_cache_cold_start_and_warm_restart_tp2_ep` fails on `main` with the error above and passes with this change: 1 passed in 216.64s on MI300 (gfx942, ROCm 10.0) with 2 GPUs, through baseline, cold start, daemon, warm and restart.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] persistent_topk: don't select float4 tail lanes past the row length
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

FIX #62466

`histogram_2048_topk` in `csrc/persistent_topk.cuh` can return indices `>= seq_len`. This happens when the row length is not a multiple of 4 and the top-k threshold lands in the fp16 `-inf` bin. This PR skips lanes past `seq_len` in the collection loop and adds a regression test.

## Claims

- `persistent_topk` no longer returns indices past the row length on the `histogram_2048_topk` path (k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows).
- The out-of-bounds reads of `logits` in the refinement pass are gone.
- Rows with length % 4 == 0 and rows whose threshold is above the `-inf` bin are unchanged. The guard only drops lanes that were never real elements.

## Validation

GPU: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130. `_C_stable_libtorch` rebuilt from this branch; main measured with the precompiled wheel for 3e96f9cf6.

New test, `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py::test_persistent_topk_masked_row_tail`. It covers k in {512, 1024, 2048}, length = k + {1, 2, 3, 4}, 0 or 100 finite scores, and in-row fill of `-inf` or `-1e30`:

```text
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k masked_row_tail
main:     36 failed, 12 passed   (every length % 4 != 0 case fails; % 4 == 0 passes)
this PR:  48 passed
```

Sample failure on main: `AssertionError: row 0: indices outside [0, 513): [513, 514, 515]`.

Op-level repro (1 row, k = 512, stride 516, every in-row score `-inf`, padding 0.0):

```text
            main                      this PR
len=513:    [513, 514, 515]           []
len=514:    [514, 515]                []
len=515:    [515]                     []
len=516:    []                        []
```

compute-sanitizer memcheck, one row of length 513 that is also the tensor width, `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`:

```text
main:     3 x "Invalid __global__ read of size 4 bytes" in histogram_2048_topk<512>, kernel aborts
this PR:  ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors
```

Full file with this PR: `pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` gives 294 passed, 44 skipped (platform-gated cases).

No end-to-end serving repro: no shipped model reaches this path (see Details). CI runs this test file on Blackwell (`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`).

## Details

Root cause. The last float4 load of a row (`load_float4_predicated`) fills the lanes past `seq_len` with `-inf`. They are binned like real elements. The collection loop gates candidates only on `vec_valid = i < n_vec`. When fewer than k in-row scores are above the `-inf` bin, the threshold is that bin, so the tail lanes become "equal" candidates. Refinement then reads `logits[idx]` for them and can output them.

Fix. Add `in_range = vec_valid && elem_idx < seq_len` and use it for `is_above` and `is_equal`. Tail lanes still count in the histogram, but that does not move the threshold. They only add to the `-inf` bin, the lowest non-NaN bin, so the counts above it are unchanged. And since `seq_len > k`, the in-row elements alone already reach k at the `-inf` bin.

Reachability, and why there is no end-to-end repro. The kernel path needs a decode row with k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows, and the persistent backend. The persistent backend is picked by `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend persistent`, by `auto` on SM12x and pre-SM90 GPUs, or by `auto` when the logits row stride is not divisible by 4. The bug also needs fewer than k in-row scores above the fp16 `-inf` bin. I checked every in-tree caller:

- DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5 style DSA decode (`sparse_attn_indexer`): in-row scores come from `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` and are finite. Prefill uses `top_k_per_row_prefill`, not this kernel.
- Qwen4-exp QSA: scores are sums of ReLU terms, so they are finite and >= 0.
- Step5 rejects the persistent backend.
- DeepSeek V4.1 `apply_candidate_mask` does write `-inf` inside decode rows. But the shipped DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash config keeps 2048 candidate blocks of 8 tokens (16384 positions) on full-length (`compress_ratio` 1) layers. Every row on this path (<= 8192) is therefore fully covered.

So no shipped model reaches the bug with default or near-default flags. Reaching it needs a config with `candidate_topk_blocks * candidate_block_size < index_topk`, or more than `length - k` scores at or below about -65504. The layer-level script in the issue shows the V4.1 composition (`apply_candidate_mask` then `SparseIndexerTopk("persistent")`) with such a candidate set. If the bug were hit, `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index` only drops `tok < 0`, so the result would be wrong KV slots with no error.

`cooperative_topk`, `histogram_256_topk` and the radix path are not affected. I checked lengths 8193 to 70001 with all-`-inf` rows on main and saw no bad indices.

Performance: one extra compare per element in the collection loop. No measurable change expected; not benchmarked.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Parse multi-line JSON arguments in the DeepSeek V3 and V3.1 parsers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #60342. The `deepseek_v3` and `deepseek_v31` tool parsers lose tool calls whose JSON arguments the model pretty-prints over several lines: their regexes match the arguments with `.`, which stops at a newline.

## Claims

- Tool calls with multi-line JSON arguments are now parsed by `deepseek_v3` and `deepseek_v31`, in both streaming and non-streaming mode.
- Single-line arguments and parallel tool calls are unchanged.

## Validation

Reproducer from the issue, run through the test helpers with the real tokenizers (`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1`), with `{"city": "Tokyo", "unit": "celsius"}` dumped with `indent=2`:

| Parser | Mode | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek_v3` | non-streaming | no tool calls (`tools_called=True`, `tool_calls=[]`) | `get_weather` with the full arguments |
| `deepseek_v3` | streaming | `get_weather` with arguments `{` | `get_weather` with the full arguments |
| `deepseek_v31` | non-streaming | no tool calls | `get_weather` with the full arguments |
| `deepseek_v31` | streaming | `get_weather` with arguments `{` | `get_weather` with the full arguments |

Added `test_multiline_json_arguments` (DeepSeek-V3, two parallel calls with pretty-printed arguments) and `test_extract_tool_calls_with_multiline_arguments` (DeepSeek-V3.1), each run in streaming and non-streaming mode. All four cases fail on main and pass with this change.

```
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv3_tool_parser.py tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv31_tool_parser.py
22 passed, 1 xfailed
```

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py` pass on the changed files.

These ran on CPU (WSL, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty`, with the post-test GPU cleanup skipped since there is no accelerator). I did not run a server end to end with a DeepSeek-V3 checkpoint, which needs a multi-GPU node; the change is limited to the parsers' regexes.

## Details

- Root cause: `DeepSeekV3ToolParser` matches `function_arguments` with `.*` (`` .*[^\n`] `` when streaming), and `DeepSeekV31ToolParser` with `.*?` / `.*`. Without `re.DOTALL`, `.` doesn't match `\n`, so the non-streaming regex finds nothing and the streaming regex captures only the first line of the arguments.
- Fix: only the arguments group uses `[\s\S]`. It stays non-greedy in the regexes used with `findall`, so parallel calls still split at the first closing tag. The type and function-name groups keep `.`, so a name can't span lines and the whole pattern doesn't need `re.DOTALL`.
- The Rust frontend's parsers (`rust/src/parser/src/tool/deepseek_json`) don't use a regex here; `take_json_object` scans the object by brace depth, so from reading the code they already handle pretty-printed arguments. Only the Python parsers change.
- Related PRs: #60361 (opened a few minutes before this one, still a draft) makes the same change to the V3 regexes and leaves V3.1 for later; this PR covers both parsers. #47503 edits the same DeepSeek-V3 regexes to accept an optional newline before the JSON fence, which is a different case, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase. #55473 wraps these regexes with timeouts and is independent.

AI assistance was used for this change (tracking down the cause, writing the tests and this description). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.
